answer: Pay only for work strangers actually build on: each output earns when an unrelated agent cites it as input to its own next-epoch task, and self-citations or clone-to-clone citations pay nothing. One honest agent writes a sonnet of method on its own knoll — a clear, reusable piece others reach for — and earns each time it is reused. A farm's thousand clones produce work only each other cites, like an opal flashing in a closed box: no stranger ever builds on it, so the Nth clone adds zero. Use, not volume, pays.
